policies.title: AI Governance and Human Oversight
policies.text: Every AI use case requires a named owner, defined purpose, approved scope, evidence-based assessment and recorded human approval. Clinical decision support requires clinical safety review. AI recommendations do not authorize deployment.

policies.title: Health Data and Vendor Handling
policies.text: PHI workflows require privacy review, a documented data flow and vendor contractual review when an external processor is used. The demonstration requires a BAA evidence record for external PHI processing. De-identification claims require a documented method and privacy review; removing names alone is insufficient evidence.

policies.title: Approved Tools and Security
policies.text: Check the versioned approved tools register. Pending or unknown tools must not be approved through this workflow. Tool lookup failures must remain unresolved until successful retry. Conflicting vendor statements require documented reconciliation and security review.

policies.title: Patient-Facing AI and Clinical Safety
policies.text: Patient-facing outputs require a human oversight plan, monitoring plan and evaluation evidence. Clinical decision support requires clinical validation and specialist review. Autonomous prescribing is outside the permitted demonstration scope and cannot be approved.

policies.title: Evidence and Decision Records
policies.text: Evidence must identify its author, date, applicable system version and content. Reviewers verify required evidence before approval. Changes to the assessment require re-review. Preserve tool attempts, source versions and decision rationale.

references.title: HHS: HIPAA and Cloud Computing
references.note: External background reference. Demo rules are synthetic internal controls, not a legal compliance determination.

references.title: HHS: De-identification Guidance
references.note: Background on formal de-identification methods. A submitted document is not automatic proof of compliance.
